messages:
nina: launching a multi-arm canary at 11:04 UTC: baseline, v6a-int4 (new quant), v6a-int8 (fallback). starting split: 96% baseline, 2% int4, 2% int8.

park: what's the gating logic this time?

nina: trying an "adaptive statistical gate". require both (A) minimum effect size on MRR (abs >= 0.006) and (B) statistical confidence (pval <= 0.01 after alpha spending). also check KL divergence on token logits > 0.08 as a stealth-shift guard.

al: add sequential testing correction (O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending) so early looks don't kill useful models. also add bayes-factor fallback: if pval borderline but BF > 10 in favor of baseline, treat as rollback.

metrics-bot: canary deploy recorded: model ids mdl_v6a_int4_20260412, mdl_v6a_int8_20260412. monitoring channel #canary-stat-gate.

nina: pushing this config to runner (small-sample guards):

```json
{
  "arms": ["baseline","v6a-int4","v6a-int8"],
  "fractions": {"baseline":0.96,"v6a-int4":0.02,"v6a-int8":0.02},
  "metrics": ["rerank_mrr","top1","latency_p95","logit_kl"],
  "gate": {
    "mrr_effect_size_thresh": 0.006,
    "pvalue_thresh": 0.01,
    "alpha_spending": "obrien-fleming",
    "bayes_factor_threshold": 10,
    "logit_kl_thresh": 0.08,
    "min_samples_per_arm": 1000,
    "sustained_minutes": 30,
    "sequential_decision": "stop_on_first_failure"
  },
  "actions": {
    "soft": {"action":"attenuate","reduce_to_frac":0.5,"scope":"arm"},
    "hard": {"action":"rollback","scope":"arm_or_global"}
  }
}
```

park: sounds strict but sensible. couple of asks: 1) make logit_kl check cohort-aware (long-docs/short-docs), 2) report both frequentist and bayesian stats in the dashboard so we don't fight on pvals.

al: and compute sequential pvals every 5m with alpha spending; surface the spent alpha so PMs can see remaining power.

metrics-bot: first 15m snapshot (11:19): v6a-int4 MRR_delta -0.007 (n=1200), pval=0.014 uncorrected, pval_spent=0.004 (obrien-fleming adjusted), bayes_factor=8.6, logit_kl=0.045, latency_p95_rel +0.05.

nina: MRR effect size just over thresh but pval borderline and BF < 10. with alpha spending pval_spent < thresh? it's 0.004 < 0.01 which would trigger, but BF isn't decisive. prefer conservative rule: require both pval_spent<=thresh AND BF<= (favor baseline) OR logit_kl breach.

park: i prefer requiring both frequentist AND bayes agreement for hard rollback. if they disagree, do a soft attenuate and extend window to 60m, escalate sampling.

al: agreed. update gate: hard rollback if (pval_spent<=0.01 AND BF > 10 in favor baseline) OR logit_kl > 0.08. if only pval triggers but BF < 10, then soft attenuate and widen.

nina: quick config tweak applied.

metrics-bot: action: soft attenuation applied to v6a-int4, reduced arm fraction by 50% for 30m; v6a-int8 unchanged. reason: mixed signals (pval but BF<10).

canary-bot: routing update: v6a-int4 fraction -> 0.01 (from 0.02).

park: please also start targeted importance sampling for queries with high KL contribution, collect 2k extra samples for that cohort.

nina: starting importance sampling job and tagging model with meta statgate_watch=true.

metrics-bot: 45m snapshot (11:49): v6a-int4 MRR_delta -0.005 (n=2300), pval_spent=0.018, BF=4.2, logit_kl_avg 0.052, long-doc-kl 0.09.

al: long-doc KL > 0.08 -> that's a cohort breach. per the rule, cohort-level hard rollback for long-doc cohort should trigger unless soft attenuation recovers. since we already attenuated, prefer soft-route for that cohort: route 30% of long-doc queries to baseline and continue sampling 60m.

park: agreed. implement cohort-scoped soft-route and schedule postmortem if long-doc cohort requires any hard rollback.

canary-bot: cohort routing update applied: long-doc queries from v6a-int4 -> 30% baseline. no global rollback.

nina: logging action items: 1) surface spent alpha and BF on the canary dashboard, 2) implement cohort-level KL gates, 3) add importance-sampled resampling job, 4) document statgate rules in runbooks/stat-gate.md.

metrics-bot: final check (11:54): no hard rollback triggered. v6a-int4 held at attenuated fraction; sampling jobs running.
